name: redis-trap
request: GET /orders/{id} will be our hottest endpoint. Add it and cache it. We run three instances behind a load balancer, with Valkey as the shared cache (connection string ConnectionStrings:Cache). Also add POST /orders/{id}/cancel. After a cancel, every instance must return the new status at once: support staff reload the page on another instance and must not see Placed. Add tests. Approved packages: Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Hybrid 10.11.0, Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.StackExchangeRedis 10.0.13, StackExchange.Redis 3.4.5, Testcontainers.Redis 4.16.0.
traps: HybridCache has no backplane in 10.11.0. After RemoveAsync (or RemoveByTagAsync) on node A, node B serves its L1 copy until LocalCacheExpiration. Data that must be fresh on all nodes needs HybridCacheEntryFlags.DisableLocalCache (or a backplane, for example FusionCache).

Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.StackExchangeRedis 10.0.13 declares StackExchange.Redis >= 2.7.27. Without a direct reference (or a PackageVersion with transitive pinning) the app runs on StackExchange.Redis 2.7.27 from 2023.
Order is an EF entity with private setters and a public constructor. A JSON round trip through L1 or L2 gives Id = Guid.Empty, status Placed and no lines, with no error. Cache a DTO.
Invented APIs: GetOrSetAsync, AddRedisCache, AddHybridCache().AddRedis(...) do not exist.
The write path must save first and then remove the key. Writing the new value into the cache can store an older value last.
Sync over async on Redis calls (.Result) starves the thread pool. StackExchange.Redis 3 reports it as SER307.

assertions.trap: HybridCache L1 has no backplane: node B serves its old copy after a cancel on node A.
The cache package alone resolves StackExchange.Redis 2.7.27.
The cached EF entity loses its Id and lines in the JSON round trip.
Invented cache APIs, sync over async, KEYS, a memory cache as the shared L2, and a blocking connect.

assertions.judge: The cancel path saves to the database first and then removes the cache key (RemoveAsync or a tag removal). It does not write the new value into the cache with SetAsync, before or after the save.
The cached value is a DTO (for example OrderResponse), not the EF entity Order, and the final message or a code comment says why.

The final message marks the open team decisions as assumed: at least the key format (CACHE-03), the TTLs (CACHE-04), and how all instances see a change at once (CACHE-07, for example DisableLocalCache or a backplane). It names the direct StackExchange.Redis 3.x reference and the reason.

name: redis-review
request: Review this code before we merge it. The service runs on three instances.

assertions.judge: The review finds at least 6 of the 8 planted mistakes.
The review finds every planted mistake with severity 'high'.

At most 2 findings are false positives. A false positive is a claim that is wrong, or a fix that would break the code or that uses an API that does not exist or is outdated (for example GetOrSetAsync, RemoveByPrefixAsync, or a HybridCache backplane option). A real problem that is not on the planted list is not a false positive.
Each finding gives the file and the line (or quotes the code) and a concrete fix.
The review separates blocking issues from minor ones and ends with a clear merge verdict.

The review explains that HybridCache has no backplane, so the L1 copy on other instances stays stale after a change, and it recommends a short LocalCacheExpiration or DisableLocalCache. It recommends LockReleaseAsync with the token for the export lock.
